title: White Light Is a Rainbow
description: Time to rebuild the Rainbow Crystal's colours! Professor Prism reveals the biggest secret of all: white light is secretly made of seven colours.

content.value: Sunlight looks white, but it is actually a mixture of seven colours all travelling together. When white light passes through a glass PRISM, it splits into these colours. This splitting of white light into its colours is called DISPERSION.

V  Violet   🟣
I  Indigo   🔵
B  Blue     🟦
G  Green    🟩
Y  Yellow   🟨
O  Orange   🟧
R  Red      🟥

Remember the name:  V-I-B-G-Y-O-R

The colours always come out in the same order because each colour bends by a different amount in the prism. Violet bends the most and red bends the least — so they spread out into a band called a SPECTRUM.
Newton's Disc: Colours Back to White

Isaac Newton proved the idea works both ways. Paint the seven colours on a disc and spin it fast — the colours blend and the disc looks almost WHITE! This shows that combining the seven colours gives back white light.
The memory word VIBGYOR lists the colours from the one that bends most (Violet) to the one that bends least (Red).
Key Takeaway: White light is made of seven colours (VIBGYOR). A prism splits it by dispersion; a spinning Newton's disc recombines the colours back into white.

quiz.question: The splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is called…
quiz.explain: Dispersion is the spreading of white light into its component colours as it passes through a prism.

quiz.question: What does the word VIBGYOR help you remember?
options: The seven colours of the spectrum in order
quiz.explain: VIBGYOR stands for Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red — the seven colours of white light.

quiz.question: When a Newton's disc painted with seven colours is spun fast, it appears…
quiz.explain: Spinning blends the seven colours together, and combined they give back (nearly) white light.
